newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Work in progress at United News.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Work in progress at United News.

text.p: United News & Media is expected to post interim pre-tax profits in excess of 100 million stg next Thursday when it reports for the first time since its three billion pound merger with MAI.
The merger was not completed until April and analysts say that the number of exceptional items likely to be included in the results makes forecasting an inexact science.
They expect pre-tax profits for the six months to June 30 to come in somewhere between 105 and 133 million stg.
The group now includes national newspaper titles and ITV television companies in southern and eastern England.

It generated combined operating profit of 269.5 million stg in 1995. Chief executive Clive Hollick said when the merger was announced that it should result in savings totalling at least 10 percent of that figure.
However, the company has warned that its performance this year will be hit by the costs of post-merger restructuring. The full benefit of the changes is not expected to feed through until 1997.
The remodelling of the group continues apace. Its Express Newspapers arm announced this week it was shedding 85 editorial jobs as it revamps its national Daily and Sunday Express titles.
The two mid-market newspapers are to be run by a single editorial team, the first time such an experiment has been attempted in Britain.
Express said that the redundancies would cost around six million stg and analysts expect a provision for this to be taken in the first half results.
United may also include some of the costs from the launch of Channel 5, the new UK commercial terrestrial television channel which will broadcast from January.
It partners Pearson, CLT of Luxembourg and Warburg Pincus of the U.S. in the Channel 5 Broadcasting consortium.

Channel 5 faces costs of around 100 million stg as it retunes video recorders in an estimated 10 million homes to avoid interference from its signal. United has announced plans to dispose of a total of 47 local newspapers in the London area and south Wales as it focuses on its strengths in regional papers in northern England. Analysts have put a price tag of around 50 million stg on the titles.
Last month it sold taxation specialist publisher Tolley to Reed Elsevier for 100.5 million stg.
The disposal of car finance company Wagon to an Abbey National subsidiary in May raised 121 million stg.
